speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Architects Act was enacted (a) to provide a framework for the registration of architects; (b) to regulate the qualifications and practice of architects; and (c) to enable the Board of Architects (BOA) to license corporations, partnerships and limited liability partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The last set of amendments to the Architects Act took effect on 1 December 2005, which included enlarging the composition of BOA and enhancing its disciplinary process.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, with globalisation, more architects are likely to provide architectural services in foreign countries and territories in addition to their country or territory of registration.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, many of our locally registered architects are well recognised for their skills and professionalism and many of them are already expanding their businesses overseas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, we need to amend the Architects Act to facilitate our locally registered architects to provide architectural services overseas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we must regulate foreign architects who provide architectural services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For locally registered architects seeking to practise overseas, they must, first, be recognised in Singapore before they engage in the practice of architecture in a participating overseas jurisdiction.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By that, we mean any country or territory outside Singapore in relation to which a mutual recognition arrangement is in force.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The need for such domestic recognition is a standard feature of the mutual recognition arrangements we have currently with various jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand have a Trilateral Agreement under the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Architect Framework.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore has also signed the ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services with other ASEAN member countries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such a domestic recognition allows for the qualifications and experience obtained by an architect in the country or territory where he or she is already registered to be recognised by the participating overseas jurisdictions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will make it easier for Singapore-registered architects to practise abroad in a participating jurisdiction and will open up opportunities for them overseas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, a foreign architect from a participating jurisdiction can be registered in Singapore to engage in the practice of architecture in Singapore, subject to the following conditions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, the foreign architect must meet the registration requirements as agreed to by BOA and the registration authority of the participating overseas jurisdiction, pass the necessary examinations as approved by BOA and also pay a prescribed fee.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The amended Act will also allow BOA to impose any prohibitions, restrictions or conditions as to the practice of architecture in Singapore when registering a foreign architect.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, BOA may impose a restriction on a foreign architect to only provide architectural services in Singapore in collaboration with a local registered architect with a valid practising certificate on a project basis, rather than doing so independently.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to clarify that an architect providing architectural services independently in Singapore as a Qualified Person is required to be a registered architect with BOA and must have a valid practising certificate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This does not change even with the amendments in this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is to avoid misleading the public that the person is authorised to provide architectural services.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will enable our Architects to operate more effectively in a globalised world and also ensure that BOA continues to play an effective role in supporting the growth of the profession.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It also expands the powers given to BOA to ensure architects in Singapore stay in line thus strengthening honest work in the profession.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I support the enhancements to the current Act and the new definitions introduced to offer clarity to the practice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Architects I have spoken to inform that industry practitioners have already been practising along these lines even before regulations were set in stone, but codifying these good practices into law is a progressive step forward.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Has there been a rise in cases in recent years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore is more advanced and sophisticated in our Building Legislation and Codes of Practice, and this Bill will now place Singapore in a better position to bring our expertise to areas which could benefit from technical support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The safeguards are different, depending on the agreements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify what is the required registration process with the Board?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Minister has mentioned this earlier, but I understand that architects from APEC have to take a domain-specific test.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In Singapore, some submissions by architects to authorities include a self-declaration to confirm that the qualified person has duly complied with the requirements from the authorities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If something goes wrong, architects may lose their licence and be removed from the Board.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If something goes wrong, for projects done by overseas architects under this "mutual recognition" scheme, what penalty would that incur?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do they lose the practice licence obtained in their country?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Training and exposure for architects in less-developed countries may not be adequate to familiarise them with Singapore's building codes and standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If there are no tight controls to limit the overseas architects to practise in Singapore, the standard of architectural practice here could be affected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Architecture is already a very competitive market with limited jobs and many firms, and some architects overseas quote cheaper fees, offering poorer quality work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, how can we offer mutual recognition, yet protect the profession in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, the Board can appoint a public officer, or any other person, to investigate offences against architects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Investigators have the power of search and require persons to provide information for investigations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify who he envisages "any other persons" to be?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, investigators should only be limited to employees of the Board, who will be more familiar with the rules and regulations.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill sets out the general qualifications and requirements for architect registration.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It brings about improvements to safeguard the interests of both the architects providing the service and the clients who sought their services.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This will, indeed, open up more opportunities for these professionals and allow them to extend their expertise and services overseas with fewer hurdles.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: At this stage, I wish to seek the following clarification on the amendments.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In regard to section 4C, if a tie occurs in the voting for the President of BOA, how will the tie be decided?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 11(2), which explains the recovery of payment from the architect, how can a person recover the amount paid to an unauthorised architect?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will he/she have to file a civil suit to recover his/her money?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As stated in section 31(k), will the appointed investigator be allowed to authorise or appoint a team of support for the investigation work?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ms K Thanaletchimi and Mr Louis Ng sought several clarifications on the administration of the Architects Act, and I will clarify the queries that they have.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And should there be another tie of votes, the successful candidate will be determined by the drawing of lots.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is already set out in the rules of the Procedure for the Election of the President of BOA.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, these rules are read out before the commencement of any voting.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Ms Thanaletchimi also sought a clarification on section 11 of the Bill, about the recovery process should the person pay money to an unauthorised architect and how would they recover the money in a Court.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The new section 15A provides for the recognition of local registered architects who intend to supply or offer to supply architectural services in any participating jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For anyone, including foreign architects who are seeking registration under section 15(1)(a) and 15(1)(b) to practise in Singapore, the qualifications recognised by BOA are already listed on its website.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They can refer to that for any clarification.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Louis Ng sought clarifications on the registration process under the new section 15(2A) for foreign architects from a participating jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, a foreign architect will need to be qualified and recognised in his/her own country, the original country or territory of registration for mutual recognition, based on the agreed criteria set out in the mutual agreements between BOA and the registration authority of the participating jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The need to pass an examination set by BOA before the foreign architect can seek registration will hence also apply to ASEAN architects recognised under the ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This was the query that Mr Louis Ng asked.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, yes, ASEAN architects will also have to take the examinations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And with these examinations, that is the way we can ensure standards are not compromised.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Louis Ng also enquired about penalties for foreign architects who are registered with BOA under the new section 15(2A), and how we can offer mutual recognition while protecting the profession in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Perhaps, I would like to explain this in two parts because there are foreign architects who qualify to practise independently in Singapore under the new section 15(2A).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These foreign architects who can qualify to practise independently will be required to maintain a valid practising certificate and they will be subjected to the same disciplinary procedures and penalties as anyone who is registered under the existing section 15(1) with a valid practising certificate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the same time, the offences committed will be reported to the foreign architect's original country or territory of registration, where the relevant authorities there will also follow up with the relevant penalties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this is for the first category of foreign architects who can qualify to practise independently.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The second category of foreign architects are those who can only practise in collaboration with a local registered architect on a project basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will not be issued a practising certificate by BOA and so they are not Qualified Persons who can offer architectural services independently in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For this category of foreign architects, in the event of a suspected offence, BOA will write to the foreign architect's original country or territory of registration.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The foreign architect will then be subjected to the investigation and disciplinary proceedings and relevant penalties imposed by the relevant authorities there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: BOA can also reject future applications from such a foreign architect to register for collaborations, depending on the seriousness of the offence committed, because a new registration for practising in collaboration with a locally registered architect is required for every new project.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if an offence is committed, BOA will take that into consideration before issuing any new registration.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Next, on the increase in penalty which is something Mr Louis Ng asked about.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This increase in the maximum penalty is to ensure that there is sufficient deterrence against any potential wrongdoings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, the higher level of penalty has also been benchmarked and is similar to that imposed by other professional boards in the medical and legal professions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Both Mr Louis Ng and Ms Thanaletchimi sought clarifications for the new section 31(K), which empowers BOA to appoint investigators to investigate into the commission of an offence under the Act.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Under the current Act, BOA will form an investigation committee which will be chaired by a Board member and comprise two other registered architects with more than 10 years of practising experience, and a layperson.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The investigation committee is in charge of evaluating the findings and making a recommendation to the Board on the investigation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is in answer to Ms Thanaletchimi's query.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With that, Madam, I beg to move.      .
